sections.title: The schema nobody owns
body: Most teams version their application code carefully and their database carelessly. Tables are created by hand, changed in a console, and documented, if at all, in a wiki page that drifted months ago.
When something breaks, nobody can say what the database is supposed to look like, only what it looks like right now.
sections.caption: Code reviewed in git, schema lost in console.

sections.title: Schema as code
body: Treat every table, view and procedure as a file in the repository. Review changes in pull requests. Let a tool work out the order to create things in, apply them, and tell you when the live database and the design disagree.
sections.caption: Every table becomes a reviewable file in folders.

sections.title: A project you can read
body: dbd is a Rust CLI and library for managing database schemas as code. You write plain SQL files; dbd handles dependency ordering, migrations, data loading, documentation and deployment.

code.text:
cargo install dbd-cli
dbd init --name myproject
dbd inspect     # validate the design
dbd apply       # apply it to $DATABASE_URL

sections.caption: Three commands order, check, and apply the schema.

sections.title: AI writes SQL faster than anyone reviews it
body: Assistants will happily generate a migration. Keeping the schema as reviewed files gives every generated change a home, a diff and a check, instead of a console session nobody saw.
sections.caption: Generated SQL lands in a pull request diff.

takeaway: Schema design that lives in your terminal.
